summary: Matthew B. Orsborn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2008–2012) under Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa. He also studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang.
Matthew Immergut is an associate professor of sociology at the State University of New York at Purchase, working in religious studies and other fields. He studied under Culadasa.

Matthew King works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto (~2009–2014) under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (~2002–2008) under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, and held a post at Lebanon Valley College around 2008.

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii (~2007–2010) and a PhD from Duke University (~2010–2016) supervised by Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Brown University (1980–1987) and held positions at the University of Chicago (1996), Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002).
Matthew Wells is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oregon (~2000–2006) under the supervision of Stephen W. Durrant.

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber (1857–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1864–1868), University of Würzburg (~1868–1890), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1890–1892).

Matthieu Ricard (born 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the Pasteur Institute (~1967–1972) under François Jacob and studied under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1979–1991).

Mattia Salvini works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (~2004–2008) under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University.

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. He served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (1879) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and William Dwight Whitney. He became a professor at Johns Hopkins University in 1881.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics, holding a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies (~1956–1978). He studied under teachers Walpola Rahula and Hammalawa Saddhatissa.
Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School (~1937–1941) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1947–1950).

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba (~-1943). She studied under traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani (~1967–1973), Eido Tai Shimano (~1969), and Soen Nakagawa (~1970–1982).

Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He served as Professor at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (~1964–1977) and Director of the Editorial Committee at the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente (~1996–2000).

Mauro Maggi is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~-1994). He held posts at the University of Hamburg (1990), Sapienza University (~2001), and IsIAO.

Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McMaster University (-1994) under Graeme MacQueen and served as Assistant Professor at United College (~1995) and Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Waterloo.

Max Deeg works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD and Habilitation from the University of Würzburg (~-1995) and was Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (~2004).

Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at Columbia University (~1889–1891). He held posts at Columbia (~1891–1892), UC Berkeley (~1897–1905), and Dropsie College (~1909–1932).
